statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of seven paths/conditions. Not covered: authenticated profile management, upload completion, payment/subscription flows, and destructive account actions because they require credentials or irreversible user data.

page.notes: Public adult video/content site with server-rendered listings, detail pages, category pages, signup, language switching, legacy jQuery/Bootstrap plugins, analytics, and third-party advertising.

artifacts.caption: Heap summary after ten login modal cycles

paths.description: Homepage and recommendation feed, representing the primary landing/listing template.
Video detail and playback page, representing the site’s core watch journey.
Amateur category page, representing taxonomy/listing templates.
Account registration page, representing the primary form and account flow.
Mobile search submission with “latina”, representing content discovery.
Deliberately unknown route, representing HTTP error and recovery handling.
English language switch, representing the localized experience.

findings.summary: Theme follows a site toggle, not the system color preference
findings.evidence: Dark and light emulation both rendered the same dark theme, and the CSS probe found no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and initialize theme colors from prefers-color-scheme, while retaining the manual override.

findings.summary: Continuous motion remains under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still returned two running 3000 ms repeating animations; only Font Awesome utility animation classes had a reduction rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential ad/carousel animation and autoplay under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not handled
findings.evidence: The CSS preference probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, while Lighthouse found footer contrast below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations and avoid fixed low-contrast brand colors for essential text and controls.

findings.summary: Navigation and carousel state use legacy abrupt/custom behavior
findings.evidence: The CSS scan found no View Transition or scroll animation timelines, while the HAR loaded Owl Carousel and Hammer.js for interaction behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route/state changes with View Transitions and prefer CSS scroll snap/scroll-driven effects over legacy gesture libraries.

findings.summary: Fixed navigation and overlays are not state or anchor aware
findings.evidence: The runtime probe found multiple fixed layers and Bootstrap role-dialog UI, but no scroll-state container query, anchor positioning, or position-try CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries for persistent chrome and CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for menus and transient UI.

findings.summary: Advertising obscures primary content
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a load-time banner plus a fixed third-party video ad and “VIEW MORE” control covering recommendation cards and video detail content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time interstitial-style ads from the content path; reserve space for ads and make any transient promotion clearly labelled and light-dismissible.

findings.summary: Dialogs and overlays use ad-hoc Bootstrap containers
findings.evidence: The DOM contained role=dialog containers but zero native dialog, popover, or details elements; Lighthouse also found the registration dialog had no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace custom modal containers with dialog/popover primitives, accessible names, focus management, and declarative light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Responsive templates do not use component-level adaptation
findings.evidence: Mobile layouts avoid overflow, but the stylesheet scan found no @container/container-type rules, leaving reusable card and navigation components tied to global breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable card grids and navigation components while preserving the current fluid fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus, touch size, and zoom support are incomplete
findings.evidence: Focused links and controls computed to outline-style none with no box shadow; Lighthouse found a 20×20 signup close control, and the viewport sets maximum-scale=1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styles, increase targets to at least 24×24 CSS px (prefer 44×44), and remove maximum-scale so users can zoom.

findings.summary: Registration errors are not programmatically actionable
findings.evidence: Empty registration submission produced a generic terms/age message, but fields had no required, aria-invalid, or aria-describedby state and no visible role=alert was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints, validate after interaction, associate field-level messages, focus the first invalid field, and announce the summary with role=alert.

findings.summary: Primary pages miss the good LCP range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 3.5 s and signup LCP 6.4 s; the trace measured homepage LCP 3.21 s. TBT stayed low, so load/resource discovery is the main bottleneck.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, shorten render-blocking chains, defer third-party media, and verify LCP below 2.5 s on both templates.

findings.summary: Image and resource delivery is wasteful
findings.evidence: The image audit found 93/94 images without dimensions, 64 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 25 oversized images, 61 without srcset, and 93 legacy-format assets. Lighthouse estimated 1,127 KiB image savings and 1,300 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Size images explicitly, emit responsive srcset/sizes, use modern formats, lazy-load below-fold media, and keep the LCP image eager with fetchpriority=high.

findings.summary: Unused CSS and JavaScript ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 62 KiB unused CSS and 69 KiB unused JavaScript; the HAR loaded legacy carousel, gesture, ad, analytics, and timezone scripts on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific code, remove unused legacy plugins, and load optional third-party behavior only after explicit user intent.

findings.summary: Core controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed menu/search buttons and links on the homepage, unnamed signup controls/selects, and an unnamed registration dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name, connect labels to fields/selects, and name dialogs with aria-labelledby.

findings.summary: Some footer text fails minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured #e4006a on #080808 at 4.29:1 for 14 px footer text, below WCAG AA 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the pink or background token to meet at least 4.5:1 and test all interactive states.

findings.summary: Zoom is restricted and video equivalents are absent
findings.evidence: The viewport uses maximum-scale=1; the detail probe found no caption tracks on either video, and Lighthouse found an undersized signup control.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow pinch zoom, provide captions/transcripts for meaningful video, and enlarge small targets.

findings.summary: Document asset hygiene has avoidable defects
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 passed, but Lighthouse found incorrect image aspect ratios and unsized images; its source-map detail also recorded a 404 map reference.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct image dimensions/aspect ratios and publish or remove stale sourceMappingURL references.

findings.summary: Localized and rich-page metadata is incomplete
findings.evidence: The English switch set lang=en but retained a Spanish title and exposed only hreflang=x-default. The video page used og:type=website and WebSite JSON-LD rather than VideoObject, and had no Twitter metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit localized titles/descriptions, reciprocal es/en hreflang URLs, HTTPS share images, and VideoObject metadata matching each video page.

findings.summary: Session transport defenses are unsafe
findings.evidence: The site is HTTPS, but CSP and HSTS are absent. PHPSESSID is neither Secure nor HttpOnly and reports SameSite=None; analytics cookies are also insecure and long-lived.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite value on the session cookie; add HSTS and a restrictive CSP, then modernize framing/referrer/permissions policies.

findings.summary: Heavy tracking and ad activity starts without visible consent
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 13 third-party origins including Google Analytics; the HAR attributed 19 requests and 943,964 bytes to third parties, including 691 KB autoplay ad media. No consent choice was visible in captured entry states.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics and advertising behind informed consent, minimize partners, partition where appropriate, and defer media until user intent.

findings.summary: Authentication lacks modern assistance
findings.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but login/signup are password-only, with no WebAuthn/passkey surface and no autocomplete tokens on email/password fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens and offer passkey registration/authentication as a phishing-resistant option.

findings.summary: A fixed third-party layer masks controls and content
findings.evidence: Across mobile templates, a fixed autoplay ad overlaps page content and controls instead of remaining in a bounded, collision-aware region.
findings.suggestedFix: Contain third-party media in reserved layout space and use collision-aware anchored/top-layer UI for transient controls.

findings.summary: The English locale remains partially Spanish and date formatting is not localized
findings.evidence: After switching to lang=en, the document title remained Spanish and partner/navigation content was mixed-language; the video detail displayed an English-style date on the Spanish route.
findings.suggestedFix: Localize document metadata and all interface strings, and format dates/numbers through Intl for the selected locale.

findings.summary: Promotional UI is visually coercive and unlabelled
findings.evidence: A fixed third-party autoplay panel with a large yellow “VIEW MORE” CTA covers site content, while tracking/advertising starts without a visible consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label advertising, never cover the primary task, avoid autoplay, and provide balanced privacy choices before non-essential processing.

findings.summary: Account fields do not support autofill or native validation
findings.evidence: Signup username/password/email fields and login email/password fields have no autocomplete tokens; signup controls are not native-required and the action is a type=button.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/new-password/email and username/current-password autocomplete tokens, native required constraints, and a semantic submit button.

findings.summary: Media and third-party bytes are disproportionate
findings.evidence: The homepage transferred 1.85 MB in the HAR, 944 KB from third parties; 93 images use legacy formats and a 341 KB animated GIF plus 691 KB ad video load immediately. Lighthouse observed 7.1 MiB in its run.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace GIF/legacy assets, serve responsive modern images, defer autoplay media, and set a template-specific byte budget.

taskList.title: Secure session cookies and deploy CSP/HSTS
Remove or defer content-obscuring ad and tracking layers
Fix accessible names, focus, zoom, targets, and video equivalents
Optimize responsive images and the critical rendering path
Make registration semantic, autofillable, and recoverable
Modernize navigation, overlays, gestures, and component responsiveness
